title.zh: 卷一百四十 列傳第六十五 崔苗二裴呂
title.en: Volume 140 Biographies 65: Cui Miao, two Pei's, Lu
title.raw: 卷一百四十 列傳第六十五 崔苗二裴呂 Volume 140 Biographies 65: Cui Miao, two Pei's, Lu

sentences.zh: 崔苗二裴呂

translations.literal: Cui, Miao, the two Peis, and Lu
translations.idiomatic: Cui, Miao, the two Peis, and Lu

translations.literal: 4.1.1 Pei Shu
translations.idiomatic: 4.1.1 Pei Shu

sentences.zh: 崔圓，字有裕，貝州武城人，後魏尚書左仆射亮八世孫。

translations.literal: Cui Yuan, styled Youyu, was a native of Wucheng in Beizhou, eighth-generation descendant of Liang, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat of Later Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuan, courtesy name Youyu, came from Wucheng in Beizhou and was the eighth-generation descendant of Liang, who had served as Left Vice Director of the Secretariat under the Northern Wei.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧，志向卓邁，喜學兵家。

translations.literal: In youth he was orphaned and poor, his aspirations lofty and far-reaching, and he delighted in studying military strategists.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor in his youth, he harbored lofty ambitions and took pleasure in studying the art of war.

sentences.zh: 開元中，詔舉遺逸，以鈐謀對策甲科，歷京兆府參軍，尹蕭炅薦之，遷會昌丞。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era, an edict summoned hidden talents; he answered on military stratagems in the first rank of the examination, served as aide in the Jingzhao prefecture, was recommended by Magistrate Xiao Jiong, and was promoted to Assistant Magistrate of Huichang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan reign, when the court called for men of talent in retirement, he placed first in the examination with a treatise on military strategy. He served as an aide in the Jingzhao prefectural office, was recommended by the magistrate Xiao Jiong, and was promoted to assistant magistrate of Huichang.

sentences.zh: 楊國忠遙領劍南節度，引圓為左司馬，知留後。

translations.literal: Yang Guozhong held the Jiannan commandery in absentia and brought Yuan in as Left Major, with charge of the rear administration.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Guozhong held the Jiannan command in absentia, he brought Yuan in as left major and put him in charge of the rear administration.

sentences.zh: 玄宗西出，次撫風，遷御史中丞、劍南節度副大使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong went west, halting at Fufeng, Yuan was moved to Censor-in-Chief and Deputy Commissioner of the Jiannan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong marched west and halted at Fufeng, Yuan was promoted to censor-in-chief and deputy commissioner of the Jiannan command.

sentences.zh: 圓銳功名，初聞難，刺國忠意，乃治城浚隍，列館宇，儲什具。

translations.literal: Yuan was keen for fame and merit; when he first heard of the crisis, he probed Guozhong's intent, then repaired the walls, deepened the moats, set up lodges, and stored supplies and equipment.
translations.idiomatic: Ambitious for fame and achievement, Yuan had just learned of the crisis when he sounded out Guozhong's intentions, then set about repairing the city walls, deepening the moats, erecting lodges, and stockpiling supplies and equipment.

sentences.zh: 帝次河池，圓疏具陳「蜀土腴穀羨，儲供易辦」。

translations.literal: When the emperor halted at Hechi, Yuan submitted a memorial fully stating that "the land of Shu is fertile and grain abundant, and provisions are easy to prepare."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor stopped at Hechi, Yuan submitted a detailed memorial arguing that "Shu has rich soil and abundant grain, and supplies there are easy to arrange."

sentences.zh: 帝省書泣下曰：「世亂識忠臣。

translations.literal: The emperor read the memorial and wept, saying: "In troubled times one knows loyal ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial and wept, saying, "It is in troubled times that loyal ministers are known.

sentences.zh: 」即日拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事，仍兼劍南節度使。

translations.literal: " That very day he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, while still holding the Jiannan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: " That same day Yuan was appointed vice director of the Secretariat and associate director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, while retaining the Jiannan command as well.

sentences.zh: 天子至，朝廷百司殿宇帷幔皆具，益嗟賞之。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven arrived, the halls, curtains, and hangings of the hundred offices of the court were all in readiness, and the emperor admired him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor arrived, the halls, curtains, and furnishings for every office of the court were already in place, and his admiration for Yuan only grew.

sentences.zh: 肅宗立，命與房琯、韋見素赴行在所，帝為製遺愛碑於蜀以寵之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong was enthroned, he ordered Yuan to go with Fang Guan and Wei Jiansu to the traveling court; the former emperor had a stele of enduring affection carved in Shu to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Suzong took the throne, Yuan was ordered to join Fang Guan and Wei Jiansu at the mobile court. The retired emperor had a stele of enduring affection erected in Shu to honor him.

sentences.zh: 至德二載，遷中書令，封趙國公，實封戶五百。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhide, he was moved to Director of the Secretariat, enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao, with five hundred households of actual fief.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Zhide era, he was promoted to director of the Secretariat, enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao with a substantive fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 乾元元年，罷為太子少師，留守東都。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianyuan, he was removed and made Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, with charge as regent of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianyuan he was dismissed from the chancellery and appointed junior tutor to the heir apparent, with responsibility as regent of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 於是上皇所置宰相無在者。

translations.literal: Thereupon none of the chancellors the Retired Emperor had appointed remained in office.
translations.idiomatic: By then none of the chancellors the retired emperor had appointed still held office.

sentences.zh: 王師之敗相州也，軍所過，皆縱剽，圓懼，委東都，奔襄陽，詔削階、封。

translations.literal: When the imperial army was defeated at Xiangzhou, wherever the troops passed they were allowed to plunder at will; Yuan was afraid, abandoned the Eastern Capital, fled to Xiangyang, and an edict stripped his rank and fief.
translations.idiomatic: After the imperial army's defeat at Xiangzhou, the troops were allowed to plunder wherever they marched. Fearing for his safety, Yuan abandoned the Eastern Capital and fled to Xiangyang, and an edict stripped him of his rank and enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 尋召拜濟王傅。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned and appointed Tutor to the Prince of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled and appointed tutor to the Prince of Ji.

sentences.zh: 李光弼表為懷州刺史，改汾州，以治行稱。

translations.literal: Li Guangbi memorialized to make him Prefect of Huaizhou; he was transferred to Fenzhou and was praised for his conduct in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi recommended him for prefect of Huaizhou, then transferred him to Fenzhou, where he won praise for the quality of his administration.

sentences.zh: 徙淮南節度使，在鎮六年，請朝京師，吏民乞留，詔檢校尚書右仆射，還之。

translations.literal: He was moved to Military Commissioner of Huainan; after six years in the post he requested audience at the capital; officials and people begged him to stay; an edict made him Acting Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and sent him back.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to military commissioner of Huainan. After six years in the post he asked to attend court in the capital, but officials and commoners pleaded that he remain. The throne appointed him acting right vice director of the Secretariat and sent him back.

sentences.zh: 久乃檢校左仆射，入知省事。

translations.literal: After a long interval he was made Acting Left Vice Director and entered to oversee Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Only after some time was he made acting left vice director and brought in to oversee Secretariat business.

sentences.zh: 大歷中卒，年六十四，贈太子太師，謚曰昭襄。

translations.literal: He died in the Dali era at sixty-four; posthumously he was given Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent, with posthumous title Zhaoxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Dali era at the age of sixty-four and was posthumously honored as grand tutor to the heir apparent, with the posthumous title Zhaoxiang.

sentences.zh: 苗晉卿

translations.literal: Miao Jinqing
translations.idiomatic: Miao Jinqing

sentences.zh: 苗晉卿，字元輔，潞州壺關人，世以儒素稱。

translations.literal: Miao Jinqing, styled Yuanfu, was a native of Huguan in Luzhou; his family was renowned for generations for scholarly simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Jinqing, courtesy name Yuanfu, came from Huguan in Luzhou. His family had been known for generations as scholars of modest means.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第，調為修武尉，累進吏部郎中、中書舍人，知吏部選事。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, was appointed Wei of Xiuwu, and rose through posts as Director in the Ministry of Personnel, Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat, with charge of personnel selection.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination he was appointed magistrate of Xiuwu and rose through the ranks to director in the Ministry of Personnel and drafting secretary of the Secretariat, with charge of civil-service selection.

sentences.zh: 選人訴索好官，厲言倨色紛於前，晉卿與相對，終日無慍顏。

translations.literal: Candidates for office pleaded and demanded good posts, harsh words and arrogant looks pressing before him; Jinqing faced them and throughout the day showed no sign of anger.
translations.idiomatic: Candidates for office pressed him with demands for desirable posts, their harsh words and arrogant manner filling the room before him, yet Jinqing faced them all day without a trace of anger.

sentences.zh: 久之，進侍郎，積寬縱，而吏下因緣作奸。

translations.literal: After a long time he was promoted to Vice Director; he grew indulgent and lax, and the clerks below took advantage to commit wrongdoing.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was promoted to vice director, but his growing leniency allowed the clerks beneath him to exploit their positions for corruption.

sentences.zh: 方時承平，選常萬人，李林甫為尚書，專國政，以銓事委晉卿及宋遙，然歲命它官同較書判，核才實。

translations.literal: At that time, in an age of peace, selections often reached ten thousand men; Li Linfu was Director and monopolized state affairs, entrusting selection affairs to Jinqing and Song Yao, yet each year other officials were ordered to compare and judge the documents and verify talent and substance.
translations.idiomatic: In those peaceful times the annual selection could involve as many as ten thousand candidates. Li Linfu, as director of the ministry, dominated state affairs and entrusted the selection process to Jinqing and Song Yao, yet each year other officials were also ordered to review the examination papers and verify candidates' true abilities.

sentences.zh: 天寶二年，判入等者凡六十四人，分甲、乙、丙三科，以張奭為第一。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianbao, those judged to have passed numbered sixty-four in all, divided into three grades of jia, yi, and bing, with Zhang Shi placed first.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianbao, sixty-four candidates were judged to have passed, divided into three grades—jia, yi, and bing—with Zhang Shi ranked first.

sentences.zh: 奭，御史中丞倚之子，倚新得幸於帝，晉卿欲附之，奭本無學，故議者囂然不平。

translations.literal: Shi was son of Censor-in-Chief Yi; Yi had newly won the emperor's favor, and Jinqing wished to attach himself to him. Shi was fundamentally without learning, so critics were loudly indignant.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was the son of Censor-in-Chief Zhang Yi, who had recently won the emperor's favor. Jinqing hoped to curry favor with the father, but Shi was utterly without learning, and critics raised a loud outcry of protest.

sentences.zh: 安祿山因間言之，帝為禦花萼樓覆實，中裁十一二，奭持紙終日，筆不下，人謂之「曳白」。

translations.literal: An Lushan seized the occasion to speak of it; the emperor held a verification at the Hua'e Tower, cutting the list by one or two in ten; Shi held the paper all day and the brush would not descend—people called it "dragging the blank."
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan seized the chance to bring the matter to the emperor's attention. The emperor held a verification examination at the Hua'e Tower and cut the passing list by roughly a tenth. Shi held his examination paper all day without setting brush to paper, and people called it "dragging the blank."

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，貶倚淮陽太守，遙武當太守，晉卿安康太守。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly enraged and demoted Yi to Prefect of Huaiyang, Yao to Prefect of Wudang, and Jinqing to Prefect of Ankang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and demoted Yi to prefect of Huaiyang, Yao to prefect of Wudang, and Jinqing to prefect of Ankang.

sentences.zh: 明年，徙魏郡，即充河北采訪使。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Weijun and at once made Commissioner for Hebei Investigation.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to Weijun and immediately appointed commissioner for Hebei investigation.

sentences.zh: 居三年，政化大行。

translations.literal: After three years in the post, government and transformation were greatly carried out.
translations.idiomatic: After three years in office his policies had taken full effect throughout the region.

sentences.zh: 嘗入計，謁歸壺關，望縣門輒步，吏諫止，晉卿以「公門當下，況父母邦乎」？

translations.literal: Once when he went in to render accounts and returned to visit Huguan, at sight of the county gate he would walk; clerks admonished him to stop, and Jinqing said, "Before the public gate one should dismount—how much more in one's parents' homeland?"
translations.idiomatic: Once, when he went to the capital to render accounts and returned to visit Huguan, he would dismount and walk at the sight of the county gate. When clerks urged him to stop, Jinqing replied, "One should dismount before the public gate—how much more so in one's native district?"

sentences.zh: 郡太守迎犒，使所屬令行酒，酒至，必立飲白釂，侍老有獻，降西階拜而飲，時美其恭。

translations.literal: The prefect of the commandery came to welcome and reward him; he had the magistrates under him pass the wine; when wine arrived he always stood, drank a full cup in one draft, and when elders offered tribute he descended the western steps, bowed, and drank—people at the time praised his reverence.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery prefect came out to welcome and entertain him. Jinqing had the magistrates under his jurisdiction pass the wine, and whenever a cup was offered he stood and drained it in a single draft. When elders came forward with offerings he descended the western steps, bowed, and drank—conduct that contemporaries praised for its reverence.

sentences.zh: 改河東郡，兼河東采訪使。

translations.literal: He was changed to Hedong commandery and concurrently made Commissioner for Hedong Investigation.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Hedong commandery and concurrently appointed commissioner for Hedong investigation.

sentences.zh: 徙撫風郡，封高平縣男。

translations.literal: He was moved to Fufeng commandery and enfeoffed as Baron of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Fufeng commandery and enfeoffed as Baron of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 遷工部尚書、東都留守。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Ministry of Works and regent of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of the Ministry of Works and appointed regent of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 召為憲部，兼左丞。

translations.literal: He was summoned to the Ministry of Justice and concurrently made Left Assistant Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the Ministry of Justice and concurrently appointed left assistant director.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，竇廷芝棄陜郡不守，楊國忠本忌其有望，即奏「東道賊沖，非大臣不可鎮遏」，授陜郡太守、陜虢防禦使，晉卿見帝，以老辭，忤旨，聽致仕於家。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, Dou Tingzhi abandoned Shaan commandery without defending it. Yang Guozhong had long resented Jinqing's prospects and at once memorialized that "the eastern route is struck by rebels and cannot be held in check except by a great minister," appointing him Prefect of Shaan and Defense Commissioner of Shan-Guo; Jinqing saw the emperor, declined on grounds of age, offended the imperial will, and was permitted to retire at home.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, Dou Tingzhi abandoned Shaan commandery without a fight. Yang Guozhong, who had long resented Jinqing's political prospects, immediately memorialized that "the eastern route is under rebel assault and only a senior minister can hold it in check," and appointed him prefect of Shaan and defense commissioner of Shan-Guo. Jinqing appeared before the emperor and declined on grounds of age, offending the throne and being permitted to retire at home.

sentences.zh: 車駕入蜀，搢紳多陷賊，晉卿間道走金州。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage entered Shu, many gentry and officials fell into the rebels' hands; Jinqing took bypaths and fled to Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial procession entered Shu, many officials fell into rebel hands, but Jinqing made his way by hidden routes to Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 晉卿寬厚，所至以惠化稱。

translations.literal: Jinqing was generous and mild; wherever he went he was praised for benevolent transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Jinqing was generous and mild-mannered, and wherever he served he was known for governing through benevolence.

sentences.zh: 魏人為營生祠，立石頌美。

translations.literal: The people of Wei built a shrine to him in life and erected a stone to praise his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Wei built a living shrine in his honor and erected a stone stele praising his virtues.

sentences.zh: 再秉政，出入七年，小心謹畏，不甚斥是非得失，故能安保寵名。

translations.literal: Twice he held the reins of government, coming and going over seven years; cautious and fearful, he did not greatly condemn right and wrong or gains and losses, and so was able to preserve favor and reputation in safety.
translations.idiomatic: He held high office twice over seven years in all, conducting himself with cautious restraint and rarely pronouncing on right and wrong or on others' gains and losses, and so was able to preserve both favor and reputation.

sentences.zh: 然練達事體，百官簿最，一省無遺，議者比漢胡廣。

translations.literal: Yet he was thoroughly versed in the substance of affairs; the registers of the hundred offices, once examined by him, left nothing omitted—critics compared him to Hu Guang of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was thoroughly versed in the substance of government business; once he reviewed the registers of the hundred offices, nothing was left unchecked, and critics compared him to Hu Guang of the Han.

sentences.zh: 肅宗欲以李輔國為常侍，奏曰：「常侍近密，非賢不可居，豈宜任等輩？

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong wished to appoint Li Fuguo as Palace Attendant; Jinqing memorialized: "The Palace Attendant is close and intimate; only the worthy may hold it—how can such a man as this be entrusted?"
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong wished to appoint Li Fuguo as palace attendant, Jinqing memorialized, "The palace attendant is a post of intimate access; only the worthy should hold it. How can a man of this sort be entrusted with it?"

sentences.zh: 」罷之。

translations.literal: " The appointment was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: " The appointment was dropped.

sentences.zh: 朝廷欲論陳希烈等死，晉卿曰：「陛下得張通儒、安守忠、孫孝哲等，何以加罪？

translations.literal: The court wished to debate sentencing Chen Xilie and others to death; Jinqing said: "Your Majesty has already obtained Zhang Tongru, An Shouzhong, Sun Xiaozhe, and the like—how can you add further punishments?"
translations.idiomatic: When the court wished to debate sentencing Chen Xilie and others to death, Jinqing said, "Your Majesty has already secured Zhang Tongru, An Shouzhong, Sun Xiaozhe, and the like—how can you add further punishments?"

sentences.zh: 」帝不從。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor did not agree.

sentences.zh: 俄而史思明亂，持是以誘眾。

translations.literal: Before long Shi Siming rebelled and used this very point to win over the masses.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Shi Siming rebelled and used this very argument to win over the people.

sentences.zh: 嘗自為父碑文，有鵲巢碑上。

translations.literal: He once composed an epitaph for his father himself, and magpies nested on the stele.
translations.idiomatic: He once composed an epitaph for his father with his own hand, and magpies nested on the stele.

sentences.zh: 賊入上黨，焚蕩略盡，而苗氏松槚獨無傷。

translations.literal: When rebels entered Shangdang they burned and ravaged nearly everything, yet the pines and cypresses of the Miao clan alone were unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels entered Shangdang they burned and ravaged nearly everything, yet the pines and cypresses at the Miao family graves alone remained unharmed.

sentences.zh: 大歷七年，配享肅宗廟廷。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Dali he was granted co-worship in Emperor Suzong's temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Dali he was granted the honor of co-worship in Emperor Suzong's temple.

sentences.zh: 十子：發、丕、堅、粲、垂、向、呂、稷、望、咸。

translations.literal: Ten sons: Fa, Pi, Jian, Can, Chui, Xiang, Lü, Ji, Wang, and Xian.
translations.idiomatic: He had ten sons: Fa, Pi, Jian, Can, Chui, Xiang, Lü, Ji, Wang, and Xian.

sentences.zh: 粲，德宗時官至郎中，陸贄欲進粲官，帝不許，曰：「晉卿往攝政，有不臣之言。

translations.literal: Can, in Emperor Dezong's time, reached the post of Director; Lu Zhi wished to advance Can in office, but the emperor would not permit it, saying: "When Jinqing formerly served as regent, he spoke words unbecoming a subject.
translations.idiomatic: Can rose to the rank of director under Emperor Dezong. When Lu Zhi wished to promote him, the emperor refused, saying, "When Jinqing formerly served as regent, he uttered words unbecoming a subject.

sentences.zh: 又名其子，皆與帝王同，粲等宜與外官。

translations.literal: He also named his sons with characters identical to those of emperors; Can and the others should receive only outer-office posts."
translations.idiomatic: He also gave his sons names that shared characters with imperial names. Can and his brothers should receive only posts outside the capital."

sentences.zh: 」贄奏：「王者爵人必於朝，刑人必於市，言與眾共之。

translations.literal: Zhi memorialized: "The king in ennobling men must do so in court, and in punishing men must do so in the market—meaning that he shares the matter with the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi memorialized in reply, "A king ennobles men only in court and punishes men only in the marketplace—that is to say, he shares such decisions with the multitude.

sentences.zh: 獎而不言其善，斯謂曲貸；

translations.literal: To reward without stating the good is what is called crooked favor;
translations.idiomatic: To reward without stating what was good is what is called crooked favor;

sentences.zh: 罰而不書其惡，斯謂中傷。

translations.literal: to punish without recording the evil is what is called slanderous injury.
translations.idiomatic: to punish without recording what was evil is what is called slanderous injury.

sentences.zh: 曲貸，則授受不明，而私幸之門啟；

translations.literal: Crooked favor makes granting and receiving unclear and opens the gate of private favor;
translations.idiomatic: Crooked favor leaves granting and receiving unclear and opens the door to private favoritism;

sentences.zh: 中傷，則枉直無辨，而讒間之道行。

translations.literal: slanderous injury leaves crooked and straight undistinguished and sets the way of calumny and estrangement in motion.
translations.idiomatic: slanderous injury leaves right and wrong undistinguished and sets calumny and estrangement in motion.

sentences.zh: 可不慎哉！

translations.literal: Can one not be cautious!
translations.idiomatic: Can one not be cautious in such matters!

sentences.zh: 若陛下以晉卿奸邪，粲等應坐，則當公議其罪；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty holds that Jinqing was treacherous and evil and that Can and the others should be implicated, then their crimes should be debated in public;
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty holds that Jinqing was treacherous and evil and that Can and his brothers should be implicated, then their crimes should be debated in public;

sentences.zh: 若知見誣，亦宜擢粲等以示天下。

translations.literal: if you know they were slandered, you should also promote Can and the others to show the empire.
translations.idiomatic: if you know they were slandered, you should also promote Can and his brothers to show the empire.

sentences.zh: 且晉卿起文儒，致位臺輔，謙柔敦厚，為三朝所推，安肯為族滅計？

translations.literal: Moreover, Jinqing rose from the literary ru, reached the highest offices, was humble, gentle, and sincere, and was commended by three reigns—how would he consent to a plan that would exterminate his clan?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Jinqing rose from the ranks of literary scholars to the highest offices, was humble, gentle, and sincere, and was commended across three reigns. How could he have entertained a plan that would have destroyed his entire clan?

sentences.zh: 雖甚狂險猶不為之，況老臣乎？

translations.literal: Even the most wildly reckless would not do such a thing—how much less an old minister?
translations.idiomatic: Even the most wildly reckless man would not have done such a thing—how much less an elderly minister?

sentences.zh: 」帝然之，而粲官終不顯。

translations.literal: " The emperor assented, yet Can's office never became prominent.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor assented, yet Can never rose to prominent office.

sentences.zh: 裴冕，字章甫，河中河東人，本冠族仕家，以蔭再調渭南尉。

translations.literal: Pei Mian, styled Zhangfu, was a native of Hedong in Hezhong; originally a leading clan in official service, through yin privilege he was twice appointed Wei of Weinan.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Mian, courtesy name Zhangfu, came from Hedong in Hezhong. Born into a leading official family, he entered service through yin privilege and was twice appointed magistrate of Weinan.

sentences.zh: 王鉷為京畿采訪使，表署判官，歷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Wang Hong was Commissioner for Jingji Investigation; Mian was entered on his staff as Administrative Aide and served through the post of Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Hong served as commissioner for Jingji investigation, Mian was entered on his staff as administrative aide and later served as palace censor.

sentences.zh: 冕少學術，然明銳，果於事，眾呈稱職，鉷雅任之。

translations.literal: Mian in youth studied the arts, yet was bright and sharp, resolute in affairs; the multitude presented him as competent, and Hong greatly trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Mian had studied the classics in his youth, yet he was bright and sharp, resolute in action, and widely regarded as competent. Hong placed great trust in him.

sentences.zh: 及鉷得罪，有詔廷辨，冕位甚下，而抗言其誣。

translations.literal: When Hong was charged with a crime, an edict ordered court debate; Mian's rank was very low, yet he spoke out against the false accusations.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong was charged with crimes, an edict ordered a court debate. Though Mian's rank was very low, he spoke out boldly against the false accusations.

sentences.zh: 鉷死，李林甫方用事，僚屬懼，皆引去，獨冕為斂葬，由是浸知名。

translations.literal: When Hong died, Li Linfu was just coming to power; his subordinates were afraid and all withdrew, but Mian alone arranged the burial, and from this gradually became known.
translations.idiomatic: After Hong died, Li Linfu was just coming to power. Hong's subordinates were afraid and all withdrew, but Mian alone arranged his burial, and from this he gradually became known.

sentences.zh: 河西節度使哥舒翰辟行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Geshu Han, Military Commissioner of Hexi, recruited him as Marching Major.
translations.idiomatic: Geshu Han, military commissioner of Hexi, recruited him as marching major.

sentences.zh: 玄宗入蜀，詔皇太子為天下兵馬元帥，拜冕御史中丞兼左庶子副之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong entered Shu, an edict made the Crown Prince Commander-in-Chief of all armies; Mian was appointed Censor-in-Chief and concurrently Left Guardian of the Heir Apparent to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong entered Shu, an edict made the crown prince commander-in-chief of all armies, and Mian was appointed censor-in-chief and concurrently left guardian of the heir apparent to assist him.

sentences.zh: 初，冕在河西，方召還，而道遇太子平涼，遂從至靈武，與杜鴻漸、崔漪同辭進曰：「主上厭於勤，且南狩蜀，宗社神器，要須有歸。

translations.literal: At first Mian was in Hexi and had just been summoned back when on the road he met the Crown Prince at Pingliang; he followed on to Lingwu and, with Du Hongjian and Cui Yi, together advanced in speech: "The sovereign is weary of toil and is moreover hunting south in Shu; the altars of state and the sacred regalia must have a destination.
translations.idiomatic: Mian had been serving in Hexi and was just being recalled when he met the crown prince on the road at Pingliang. He followed on to Lingwu and, together with Du Hongjian and Cui Yi, advanced this argument: "The sovereign is weary of rule and is retreating south into Shu. The altars of state and the sacred regalia must find a home.

sentences.zh: 今天意人事，屬在殿下，宜正位號。

translations.literal: Now Heaven's intent and human affairs belong to Your Highness; you should rectify your title and designation.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's intent and the affairs of men now rest with Your Highness. You should assume the imperial title.

sentences.zh: 有如逡巡，失億兆心，則大事去矣。

translations.literal: If you hesitate and lose the hearts of the hundred millions, the great affair will be lost.
translations.idiomatic: If you hesitate and lose the hearts of the multitude, the great enterprise will be lost.

sentences.zh: 」太子曰：「我平寇逆，奉迎乘輿還京師，退居涼貳，以侍膳左右，豈不樂哉！

translations.literal: " The Crown Prince said: "I shall pacify the rebels, welcome the imperial carriage back to the capital, withdraw to the cool second rank, and attend at meals left and right—how could that not be joy!
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince replied, "I shall pacify the rebels, welcome the imperial carriage back to the capital, withdraw to the secondary position, and attend my father at table—what could be more welcome!

sentences.zh: 公等何言之過！

translations.literal: How excessive are your words!"
translations.idiomatic: How excessive are your words!"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「殿下居東宮二十年，今多難啟聖，以安社稷，而所從將士皆關輔人，日夜思歸，大眾一騷，不可復集，不如因而撫之，以就大功。

translations.literal: " They replied: "Your Highness has dwelt in the Eastern Palace twenty years; now in many difficulties you should inaugurate sagely rule to settle the altars of state. Yet the officers and soldiers who follow you are all men of Guanfu; day and night they think of returning home. Once the great host is stirred, it cannot be gathered again—better to take advantage and reassure them to accomplish the great merit.
translations.idiomatic: " They replied, "Your Highness has dwelt in the Eastern Palace for twenty years. Now, in this time of many calamities, you should inaugurate sagely rule to secure the altars of state. Yet the officers and soldiers who follow you are all men of the Guanzhong region; day and night they think of returning home. Once the great host is stirred, it cannot be gathered again. Better to reassure them now and accomplish the great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 臣等昧死請。

translations.literal: We your subjects beg in ignorance of death."
translations.idiomatic: We your subjects beg this at the risk of our lives."

sentences.zh: 」太子固讓，凡五請，卒見聽。

translations.literal: " The Crown Prince firmly declined; in all they requested five times, and in the end he was persuaded.
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince firmly declined, but after five entreaties he at last consented.

sentences.zh: 太子即位，進冕中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince took the throne, Mian was advanced to Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince took the throne, Mian was promoted to vice director of the Secretariat and associate director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 乃建言賣官、度僧道士，收貲濟軍興。

translations.literal: He then proposed selling offices and ordaining monks and Daoist priests, collecting fees to supply military expenses.
translations.idiomatic: He then proposed selling offices and ordaining monks and Daoist priests, collecting fees to fund the war effort.

sentences.zh: 時取償既賤，眾不為宜。

translations.literal: At the time the compensation taken was so cheap that the multitude did not consider it proper.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the fees collected were so low that most people regarded the policy as improper.

sentences.zh: 肅宗至鳳翔，罷冕政事，拜尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong reached Fengxiang, Mian was removed from government affairs and appointed Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong reached Fengxiang, Mian was removed from government affairs and appointed right vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 兩京平，封冀國公，實封五百戶，出為劍南西川節度使。

translations.literal: When the two capitals were pacified, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Ji with five hundred households of actual fief and sent out as Military Commissioner of Jiannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After the two capitals were recovered, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Ji with a substantive fief of five hundred households and sent out as military commissioner of Jiannan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 復為右僕射，待制集賢院。

translations.literal: He was again made Right Vice Director and awaited edicts at the Academy of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed right vice director and served awaiting edicts at the Academy of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 俄充山陵使。

translations.literal: Before long he was made Commissioner for the Imperial Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed commissioner for the imperial mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 於是，中書舍人劉烜為李輔國所昵，冕表為判官。

translations.literal: Thereupon Drafting Secretary Liu Xuan was favored by Li Fuguo, and Mian memorialized to make him Administrative Aide.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the drafting secretary Liu Xuan was favored by Li Fuguo, and Mian memorialized to appoint him as his administrative aide.

sentences.zh: 烜抵法，坐降施州刺史，徙澧州。

translations.literal: Xuan was brought to law and, on that account, demoted to Prefect of Shi and moved to Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was brought to trial and, on that account, demoted to prefect of Shi and later transferred to Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，郭子儀言於代宗曰：「冕首佐先帝，馳驅靈武，有社稷勛，程元振忌其賢，遂加誣構，海內冤之。

translations.literal: In the Dali era Guo Ziyi spoke to Emperor Daizong: "Mian was the first to assist the late emperor, galloping to Lingwu; he had merit for the altars of state. Cheng Yuanzhen envied his worth and thereupon added false constructions; within the seas all felt it unjust."
translations.idiomatic: During the Dali era Guo Ziyi said to Emperor Daizong, "Mian was among the first to assist the late emperor, riding in haste to Lingwu, and he earned merit for the altars of state. Cheng Yuanzhen envied his talent and fabricated charges against him, and the empire regarded it as a grave injustice."

sentences.zh: 陛下宜還冕於朝，復俾輔相，必能致治成化。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should return Mian to court, again make him chancellor, and he will surely bring order and complete transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should recall Mian to court and again appoint him chancellor; he will surely bring order and complete the work of transformation.

sentences.zh: 」時元載秉政，冕早所甄引，載德之，又貪其衰瘵，且下己，遂拜左僕射、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: " At that time Yuan Zai held the government; Mian had long ago been selected and promoted by him; Zai was grateful to him, and also coveted his decline and infirmity, and that he was beneath himself—thereupon he was appointed Left Vice Director and Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time Yuan Zai held power. Mian had long ago been selected and promoted by him; Zai was grateful and also took comfort in Mian's age and infirmity, confident that Mian stood beneath him. Mian was thereupon appointed left vice director and associate director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 入見，拜不能興，載自扶之，代為贊謝。

translations.literal: On entering audience he could not rise in bowing; Zai himself supported him and answered thanks on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: When he entered audience he could not rise to bow; Zai himself supported him and answered the emperor's thanks on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 俄兼河南江淮副元帥、東都留守。

translations.literal: Before long he was concurrently made Deputy Commander-in-Chief for Henan and the Jiang-Huai region and regent of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was concurrently appointed deputy commander-in-chief for Henan and the Jiang-Huai region and regent of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 不逾月卒，有詔贈太尉。

translations.literal: In less than a month he died; an edict posthumously gave him Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Within less than a month he died, and an edict posthumously honored him as grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 冕以忠勤自將，然不知宰相大體。

translations.literal: Mian conducted himself with loyalty and diligence, yet did not understand the great substance of the chancellor's role.
translations.idiomatic: Mian conducted himself with loyalty and diligence, yet he did not understand the larger responsibilities of a chancellor.

sentences.zh: 性豪侈，既素貴，輿服食飲皆光麗珍豐，櫪馬直數百金者常十數，每廣會賓客，不能名其饌，自製巾子工甚，人爭效之，號「僕射巾」。

translations.literal: By nature extravagant, since he had long been noble his carriage, food, drink, and clothing were all lustrous, fine, and abundant; horses in the stable worth several hundred cash each numbered regularly more than ten; whenever he gave broad feasts for guests he could not name the dishes; the turban he made himself was very skillfully wrought, and people vied to imitate it, calling it the "Vice Director's turban."
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was extravagant. Long accustomed to wealth and rank, his carriage, dress, food, and drink were all splendid and lavish. He regularly kept more than ten horses in his stable worth several hundred strings of cash each. Whenever he gave grand feasts for guests he could not even name every dish served. The turban he designed himself was exquisitely made, and people vied to imitate it, calling it the "Vice Director's turban."

sentences.zh: 領使既眾，吏白俸簿月二千緡，冕顧視，喜見顏間，世訾其嗜利云。

translations.literal: The commissions he held were many; clerks reported that his salary registers came to two thousand strings of cash per month; Mian looked them over and pleasure showed on his face—later ages reviled his love of profit.
translations.idiomatic: With so many concurrent commissions, clerks reported that his monthly salary registers totaled two thousand strings of cash. Mian looked them over and pleasure showed plainly on his face, and later ages reviled his love of profit.

sentences.zh: 始，肅宗廟惟苗晉卿配享，冕卒後二十餘年，有蘇正元者奏言：「肅宗為元帥時，師才一旅，冕於草創中，甄大義以勸進，收募驍勇幾十餘萬。

translations.literal: At first in Emperor Suzong's temple only Miao Jinqing received co-worship; more than twenty years after Mian's death, one Su Zhengyuan memorialized: "When Emperor Suzong was Commander-in-Chief, his army was barely one brigade; Mian, amid founding efforts, discerned the great principle to urge enthronement and gathered and recruited fierce warriors to nearly a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: At first only Miao Jinqing received co-worship in Emperor Suzong's temple. More than twenty years after Mian's death, a man named Su Zhengyuan memorialized, saying, "When Emperor Suzong served as commander-in-chief, his army was barely one brigade strong. Amid the founding struggle, Mian discerned the great principle and urged enthronement, gathering and recruiting fierce warriors to nearly a hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 既逾月，房琯來；

translations.literal: After more than a month Fang Guan came;
translations.idiomatic: More than a month later Fang Guan arrived;

sentences.zh: 又一年，而晉卿至。

translations.literal: after another year Jinqing arrived.
translations.idiomatic: and a year after that Jinqing arrived.

sentences.zh: 今晉卿從祀，而冕乃不與。

translations.literal: Now Jinqing follows in sacrifice, yet Mian is not included.
translations.idiomatic: Now Jinqing shares in sacrifice, yet Mian does not.

sentences.zh: 」有詔冕配享肅宗廟。

translations.literal: " An edict granted Mian co-worship in Emperor Suzong's temple.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict granted Mian co-worship in Emperor Suzong's temple.

sentences.zh: 裴遵慶

translations.literal: Pei Zunqing
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zunqing

sentences.zh: 裴遵慶，字少良，絳州聞喜人。

translations.literal: Pei Zunqing, styled Shaoliang, was a native of Wenxi in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zunqing, courtesy name Shaoliang, came from Wenxi in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 幼強學，該綜圖傳，外晦內明，不幹當世。

translations.literal: In youth he studied strenuously, mastered charts and records comprehensively, was outwardly obscure yet inwardly bright, and did not meddle with the age.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied strenuously and mastered charts and historical records comprehensively. Outwardly retiring yet inwardly sharp, he did not meddle in worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 年既長，始以仕家推蔭為興寧陵丞，調大理丞。

translations.literal: When his years had grown, he first entered office through the yin privilege of his official family as Assistant of Xingning Mausoleum, and was transferred to Aide in the Court of Review.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he first entered office through his family's yin privilege as assistant of Xingning Mausoleum, then was transferred to aide in the Court of Review.

sentences.zh: 邊將蕭克濟督役苛暴，役者有醜言，有司以大逆論，遵慶曰：「財不足聚人，力不足加眾，焉能反？

translations.literal: The frontier general Xiao Keji supervised labor with harsh cruelty; the laborers had ugly words, and the authorities judged it as great treason. Zunqing said: "Without wealth one cannot gather men, without strength one cannot overcome the multitude—how could they rebel?"
translations.idiomatic: The frontier general Xiao Keji supervised labor with harsh cruelty, and the laborers spoke rebellious words. When the authorities judged the case as great treason, Zunqing said, "Without wealth one cannot gather followers, and without strength one cannot overcome the multitude. How could they rebel?"

sentences.zh: 」由是全救數十族。

translations.literal: " Thereby he wholly saved several tens of clans.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereby he saved several dozen families in all.

sentences.zh: 頻擢吏部員外郎，判南曹。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Director in the Ministry of Personnel and judged the Southern Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to director in the Ministry of Personnel with charge of the Southern Bureau.

sentences.zh: 天寶時，選者歲萬計，遵慶性強敏，視簿牒，詳而不苛，世稱吏事第一。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era candidates for selection numbered tens of thousands each year; Zunqing was by nature forceful and keen, and in reviewing registers he was thorough without harshness—his age called him first in clerical affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao era annual selections could involve tens of thousands of candidates. Zunqing was by nature forceful and keen; in reviewing registers he was thorough without harshness, and his age called him first in clerical affairs.

sentences.zh: 肅宗時，為吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In Emperor Suzong's time he was Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Suzong he served as vice director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 蕭華輔政，屢薦之，拜黃門侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Xiao Hua assisted in government and repeatedly recommended him; he was appointed Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat and Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Hua assisted in government he repeatedly recommended Zunqing, who was appointed vice director of the Palace Secretariat and associate director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 代宗初，仆固懷恩反，帝以遵慶忠厚大臣，故奉詔宣慰，懷恩聽命將入朝，既而為其將范志誠沮止。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Daizong's reign Pugu Huai'en rebelled; the emperor, because Zunqing was a loyal and sincere great minister, ordered him to proclaim consolation; Huai'en obeyed and was about to enter court, but was then stopped by his general Fan Zhicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Daizong's reign Pugu Huai'en rebelled. Because Zunqing was a loyal and sincere senior minister, the emperor sent him with an edict to proclaim consolation. Huai'en obeyed and was about to enter court, but was then stopped by his general Fan Zhicheng.

sentences.zh: 時帝在陜，遵慶脫身赴行在。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor was in Shan; Zunqing escaped and hurried to the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then at Shan, and Zunqing escaped and hurried to the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 帝還，遷太子少傅。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned, he was moved to Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to the capital, Zunqing was promoted to junior tutor to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 罷為集賢院待制，改吏部尚書，以尚書右僕射復知選事，朝廷優其老，聽就第註官，時以為榮。

translations.literal: He was removed and made Awaiting Edicts at the Academy of Assembled Worthies, changed to Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and as Right Vice Director of the Secretariat again took charge of selection affairs; the court favored his age and permitted him to register appointments at his residence—people at the time regarded it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: He was removed from the chancellery and made awaiting edicts at the Academy of Assembled Worthies, then appointed director of the Ministry of Personnel. As right vice director of the Secretariat he again took charge of selection affairs. The court favored his age and permitted him to register appointments from his residence, which contemporaries regarded as a signal honor.

sentences.zh: 嘗有族子病狂易，告以謀反，帝識其謬，置不問。

translations.literal: Once a clansman's son, sick with mania, reported that Zunqing was plotting rebellion; the emperor recognized the absurdity and set the matter aside.
translations.idiomatic: Once a clansman's son, sick with mania, reported that Zunqing was plotting rebellion. The emperor recognized the absurdity and set the matter aside.

sentences.zh: 性惇正，老而彌謹。

translations.literal: By nature sincere and upright, in old age he became all the more cautious.
translations.idiomatic: By nature sincere and upright, he became all the more cautious in old age.

sentences.zh: 每薦賢，有來謝者，以為恥。

translations.literal: Whenever he recommended the worthy, if anyone came to thank him he regarded it as shame.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he recommended the worthy, he regarded it as shameful if anyone came to thank him.

sentences.zh: 諫而見從，即內益畏。

translations.literal: When he remonstrated and was followed, inwardly he grew all the more fearful.
translations.idiomatic: When he remonstrated and the emperor followed his advice, inwardly he grew all the more fearful.

sentences.zh: 雖親近，但記其削稿疏數，而莫知所言。

translations.literal: Even those close to him only noted the number of his draft memorials, and did not know what he had said.
translations.idiomatic: Even those close to him noted only the number of his draft memorials and did not know what he had written.

sentences.zh: 大歷十年薨，年九十餘。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Dali he died at more than ninety.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the tenth year of Dali at more than ninety years of age.

sentences.zh: 初為郎時，著《王政記》，述今古治體，識者知其有公輔器云。

translations.literal: When he first served as a Gentleman he composed Records of Royal Government, setting forth the governing substance of past and present; those who knew him recognized that he had the capacity of a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: When he first served as a gentleman he composed Records of Royal Government, setting forth the principles of governance past and present. Those who knew him recognized that he had the capacity of a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 子向。

translations.literal: His son was Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Xiang.

sentences.zh: 向字傃仁，以蔭得調。

translations.literal: Xiang, styled Suren, entered office through yin privilege.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang, courtesy name Suren, entered office through yin privilege.

sentences.zh: 建中初，李紓為同州刺史，奏署判官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianzhong, Li Shu was Prefect of Tongzhou and entered him on staff as Administrative Aide.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianzhong era, when Li Shu was prefect of Tongzhou, he entered Xiang on his staff as administrative aide.

sentences.zh: 李懷光叛河中，使其將趙貴先築壘於同州，紓奔奉天，而向領州務。

translations.literal: Li Huai'guang rebelled in Hezhong and sent his general Zhao Guixian to build ramparts at Tongzhou; Shu fled to Fengtian, while Xiang took charge of prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Huai'guang rebelled in Hezhong he sent his general Zhao Guixian to build fortifications at Tongzhou. Shu fled to Fengtian, while Xiang took charge of prefectural affairs.

sentences.zh: 貴先脅吏督役，不及期，將斬以徇，民皆駭散，向獨詣貴先壘開諭之，貴先乃降。

translations.literal: Guixian coerced clerks to supervise labor; when the deadline was not met he was about to behead someone as an example, and the people were all terrified and scattered; Xiang alone went to Guixian's rampart and opened persuasion, and Guixian thereupon surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Guixian coerced clerks to supervise labor, and when the deadline was not met he was about to behead a man as an example, terrifying the people into flight. Xiang alone went to Guixian's camp and persuaded him to surrender, which Guixian then did.

sentences.zh: 同州不陷，向力也。

translations.literal: That Tongzhou did not fall was Xiang's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: That Tongzhou did not fall was Xiang's achievement.

sentences.zh: 累為櫟陽、渭南令，奏課皆第一，擢戶部員外郎。

translations.literal: He served repeatedly as Magistrate of Liyang and Weinan; in all memorial reports of performance he ranked first and was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He served repeatedly as magistrate of Liyang and Weinan, ranking first in every performance report, and was promoted to director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 德宗末，方鎮之副，多自選於朝，以待有變，次授之，故向以選為太原少尹、行軍司馬，歷陜虢觀察使，以吏部尚書致仕。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Dezong's reign, deputies of the regional commands were mostly chosen from the court to await changes and then assigned in turn; thus Xiang through selection became Junior Magistrate of Taiyuan and Marching Major, served as Commissioner for Observation of Shan-Guo, and retired as Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Emperor Dezong's reign, deputies for the regional commands were mostly chosen from the capital to await assignment when changes arose. Xiang was selected as junior magistrate of Taiyuan and marching major, later served as commissioner for observation of Shan-Guo, and retired as director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 向能以學行持門戶，內外親屬百餘口，祿俸必均，世稱其孝睦。

translations.literal: Xiang was able through learning and conduct to uphold the household gate; within and without, close kin numbered more than a hundred mouths, and salaries and stipends were always divided equally—his age praised his filial piety and harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang upheld his household through learning and conduct. Among his close kin within and without the family there were more than a hundred mouths, and he always divided salaries and stipends equally. His age praised his filial piety and harmony.

sentences.zh: 卒年八十，贈太子少保。

translations.literal: He died at eighty and was posthumously given Junior Guardian to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty and was posthumously honored as junior guardian to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 子寅，官累御史大夫。

translations.literal: His son Yin rose through offices to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yin rose through the ranks to censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 寅子樞。

translations.literal: Yin's son was Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Yin's son was Shu.

sentences.zh: 樞字紀聖，咸通中，第進士。

translations.literal: Shu, styled Jisheng, in the Xiantong era passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Shu, courtesy name Jisheng, passed the jinshi examination during the Xiantong era.

sentences.zh: 杜審權鎮河中，奏署幕府，再遷藍田尉。

translations.literal: Du Shenquan held Hezhong and entered him on the staff; he was twice moved to Wei of Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Shenquan held Hezhong he entered Shu on his staff, and Shu was twice promoted to magistrate of Lantian.

sentences.zh: 宰相王鐸知之，遂直弘文館。

translations.literal: Chancellor Wang Duo knew his worth and had him serve directly at the Hongwen Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Wang Duo recognized his talent and had him serve directly at the Hongwen Academy.

sentences.zh: 鐸罷，樞久不調。

translations.literal: When Duo was removed, Shu long went without reassignment.
translations.idiomatic: After Duo was dismissed, Shu went long without reassignment.

sentences.zh: 從僖宗入蜀，擢殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Xizong into Shu and was promoted to Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Xizong into Shu and was promoted to palace censor.

sentences.zh: 中和初，鐸為都統，表署鄭滑掌書記。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhonghe, Duo was Commander-in-Chief and entered him on staff as Secretary of Zheng-Hua.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhonghe era, when Duo served as commander-in-chief, he entered Shu on staff as secretary of Zheng-Hua.

sentences.zh: 龍紀初，進給事中，改京兆尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longji he was advanced to Drafting Attendant and changed to Magistrate of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Longji era he was advanced to drafting attendant and appointed magistrate of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 與孔緯厚善，緯以罪貶，故樞改右庶子，出為歙州刺史。

translations.literal: He was thick friends with Kong Wei; when Wei was demoted for a crime, Shu was therefore changed to Right Guardian of the Heir Apparent and sent out as Prefect of Shezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was close friends with Kong Wei. When Wei was demoted for a crime, Shu was transferred to right guardian of the heir apparent and sent out as prefect of Shezhou.

sentences.zh: 遷右散騎常侍，為汴州宣諭使。

translations.literal: He was moved to Right Regular Cavalier Attendant and made Commissioner to Proclaim Consolation at Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right regular cavalier attendant and appointed commissioner to proclaim consolation at Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 樞素與朱全忠相結納，故全忠聽命，修貢獻不絕。

translations.literal: Shu had long been bound in alliance with Zhu Quanzhong, so Quanzhong obeyed orders and continuously sent tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Shu had long been allied with Zhu Quanzhong, so Quanzhong obeyed imperial orders and continuously sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 昭宗悅，遷兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong was pleased and moved him to Vice Director of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozong was pleased and promoted him to vice director of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 時崔胤亦倚全忠專朝柄，因與樞善。

translations.literal: At the time Cui Yin also relied on Quanzhong to monopolize court power, and therefore was on good terms with Shu.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Cui Yin also relied on Quanzhong to monopolize court power and therefore was on good terms with Shu.

sentences.zh: 俄以戶部侍郎同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Before long he was made Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue and Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed vice director of the Ministry of Revenue and associate director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 帝在鳳翔，貶胤官，樞亦罷為工部尚書。

translations.literal: When the emperor was at Fengxiang, Yin was demoted in office and Shu was also removed and made Director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was at Fengxiang, Yin was demoted and Shu was also removed from the chancellery and made director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 已還宮，拜檢校尚書右仆射、同平章事。

translations.literal: After returning to the palace he was appointed Acting Right Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor returned to the palace, Shu was appointed acting right vice director of the Secretariat and associate director of the chancellery.

sentences.zh: 出為清海節度使。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Military Commissioner of Qinghai.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as military commissioner of Qinghai.

sentences.zh: 全忠言樞有經世才，不宜棄外，復拜門下侍郎平章事，監修國史。

translations.literal: Quanzhong said Shu had talent to order the age and should not be abandoned abroad; he was again appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery and Associate Director, with charge of compiling the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong said Shu had talent to govern the age and should not be abandoned in the provinces. He was recalled as vice director of the Secretariat-chancellery and associate director, with charge of compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 累進右僕射、諸道鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly advanced to Right Vice Director and Commissioner for Salt and Iron Transport of all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to right vice director and commissioner for salt and iron transport of all circuits.

sentences.zh: 哀帝嗣位，柳璨方用事，全忠以牙將張廷範為太常卿，樞以為廷範勛臣，自宜任方鎮，何用為卿，恐非王意，持不下。

translations.literal: When Emperor Aidi succeeded, Liu Can was just coming to power; Quanzhong made his military officer Zhang Tingfan Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. Shu held that Tingfan, as a meritorious minister, ought naturally to hold a regional command—what use was there in making him Director? He feared this was not the king's intent and withheld approval.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Aidi succeeded, Liu Can was coming to power. Quanzhong appointed his military officer Zhang Tingfan director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. Shu held that Tingfan, as a meritorious minister, ought naturally to hold a regional command rather than such a court post, and feared this was not the emperor's intent. He withheld approval.

sentences.zh: 全忠怒謂賓佐曰：「吾常器樞不浮薄，今乃爾。

translations.literal: Quanzhong angrily told his guests and aides: "I always valued Shu as not shallow and frivolous—now he is like this."
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong angrily told his staff, "I always valued Shu as a man of substance, not shallow and frivolous. Now he proves otherwise."

sentences.zh: 」璨聞，即罷樞政事，拜左僕射。

translations.literal: " Can heard of it and at once removed Shu from government affairs, appointing him Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: " When Can heard of it he at once removed Shu from government affairs and appointed him left vice director.

sentences.zh: 俄貶登州刺史，又貶瀧州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: Before long he was demoted to Prefect of Dengzhou, then again demoted to Registrar of Longzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was demoted to prefect of Dengzhou, then again demoted to registrar of Longzhou.

sentences.zh: 至滑州，全忠遣人殺之白馬驛，投屍於河，年六十五。

translations.literal: When he reached Huazhou, Quanzhong sent men to kill him at Baima Post, casting his corpse into the river; he was sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Huazhou, Quanzhong sent men to kill him at Baima Post and cast his corpse into the river. He was sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 初，全忠佐吏李振曰：「此等自謂清流，宜投諸訶，永為濁流。

translations.literal: At first Quanzhong's aide Li Zhen said: "These men call themselves the clear current; they should be cast into the He River and forever become the muddy current."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Quanzhong's aide Li Zhen had said, "These men call themselves the clear current. They should be cast into the He River and forever become the muddy current."

sentences.zh: 」全忠笑而許之。

translations.literal: " Quanzhong laughed and assented.
translations.idiomatic: " Quanzhong laughed and assented.

sentences.zh: 呂諲，河中河東人。

translations.literal: Lü Yin was a native of Hedong in Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Yin came from Hedong in Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 少力於學，志行整飭。

translations.literal: In youth he strove in study; his aims and conduct were orderly and disciplined.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he strove in study, and his aims and conduct were orderly and disciplined.

sentences.zh: 孤貧不自業，裏人程氏財雄於鄉，以女妻諲，亦以諲才不久困，厚分貲贍濟所欲，故稱譽日廣。

translations.literal: Orphaned and poor, he could not support himself; a village man of the Cheng clan was wealthy and powerful in the district and gave him his daughter in marriage, also believing that with Yin's talent he would not long remain in hardship; he generously divided wealth to supply what Yin desired, and so his reputation daily grew.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor, he could not support himself. A village man of the Cheng clan, wealthy and powerful in the district, gave him his daughter in marriage, believing that with Yin's talent he would not long remain in hardship. The Cheng family generously supplied his needs, and his reputation steadily grew.

sentences.zh: 開元末，入京師，第進士，調寧陵尉，采訪使韋陟署為支使。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaiyuan he entered the capital, passed the jinshi examination, was appointed Wei of Ningling, and Commissioner Wei Zhi entered him on staff as Branch Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Kaiyuan era he entered the capital, passed the jinshi examination, was appointed magistrate of Ningling, and was entered on the staff of Commissioner Wei Zhi as branch commissioner.

sentences.zh: 哥舒翰節度河西，表支度判官。

translations.literal: Geshu Han was Military Commissioner of Hexi and memorialized him as Administrative Aide for Supplies.
translations.idiomatic: When Geshu Han served as military commissioner of Hexi he memorialized Yin as administrative aide for supplies.

sentences.zh: 歷太子通事舍人。

translations.literal: He served through the post of Communications Secretary to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He served as communications secretary to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 性靜慎，勤總吏職，諸僚或出遊，諲獨頹然據案，鉤視簿最，翰益親之。

translations.literal: By nature quiet and cautious, diligent in summing up clerical duties, when his colleagues went out on excursions Yin alone sat bent over the desk, checking and reviewing registers; Han grew all the more intimate with him.
translations.idiomatic: By nature quiet and cautious, he was diligent in clerical duties. When his colleagues went out on excursions Yin alone sat bent over his desk checking registers, and Han grew all the more intimate with him.

sentences.zh: 累兼殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He repeatedly served concurrently as Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly served concurrently as palace censor.

sentences.zh: 翰敗潼關，諲西趨靈武，由中人尉薦，肅宗才之，拜御史中丞，所陳事無不順納。

translations.literal: When Han was defeated at Tong Pass, Yin hurried west to Lingwu; through recommendation by the eunuch Wei, Emperor Suzong recognized his talent and appointed him Censor-in-Chief; whatever he presented was without exception accepted.
translations.idiomatic: When Han was defeated at Tong Pass, Yin hurried west to Lingwu. Through recommendation by the eunuch Wei, Emperor Suzong recognized his talent and appointed him censor-in-chief. Whatever he presented was accepted without exception.

sentences.zh: 從至鳳翔，遷武部侍郎。

translations.literal: He followed on to Fengxiang and was moved to Vice Director of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the emperor to Fengxiang and was promoted to vice director of the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 帝復兩京，詔盡系群臣之汙賊者，以御史中丞崔器、憲部侍郎韓擇木、大理卿嚴向為三司使處其罪，又詔御史大夫李峴及諲領使。

translations.literal: When the emperor recovered the two capitals, an edict ordered that all officials who had stained themselves by serving the rebels be imprisoned; Censor-in-Chief Cui Qi, Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice Han Zemu, and Director of the Court of Review Yan Xiang were made the Three Offices commissioners to dispose their crimes; another edict ordered Censor-in-Chief Li Xian and Yin to lead the commission.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor recovered the two capitals, an edict ordered that all officials who had served the rebels be imprisoned. Censor-in-chief Cui Qi, vice director of the Ministry of Justice Han Zemu, and director of the Court of Review Yan Xiang were appointed commissioners of the Three Offices to dispose their crimes. Another edict ordered censor-in-chief Li Xian and Yin to lead the commission.

sentences.zh: 諲於權宜知大體不及峴，而援律傅經過之，當時憚其持法，然以峴故，多所平反。

translations.literal: Yin in expedient policy and knowledge of the great substance did not match Xian, yet in citing law and applying the classics he went too far; people at the time feared his enforcement of law, yet because of Xian many cases were reversed.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was inferior to Xian in expedient policy and grasp of larger principles, yet in citing law and applying the classics he went too far. Contemporaries feared his strict enforcement of law, yet because of Xian many cases were reversed.

sentences.zh: 乾元二年，九節度兵敗，帝憂之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianyuan the nine military commissioners' armies were defeated, and the emperor was troubled.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qianyuan the armies of the nine military commissioners were defeated, and the emperor was deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 擢諲同中書門下平章事，知門下省，翌日，復以李峴、李揆、第五琦為宰相，而苗晉卿、王玙罷。

translations.literal: Yin was promoted to Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery with charge of the Secretariat-Chancellery office; the next day Li Xian, Li Kui, and Diwu Qi were again made chancellors, while Miao Jinqing and Wang Yu were removed.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was promoted to associate director of the Secretariat-Chancellery with charge of the Secretariat office. The next day Li Xian, Li Kui, and Diwu Qi were again appointed chancellors, while Miao Jinqing and Wang Yu were removed.

sentences.zh: 會母喪解，三月復召知門下省事，兼判度支，還執政。

translations.literal: He met his mother's mourning and left office; after three months he was again summoned to oversee Secretariat affairs and concurrently judge the Ministry of Revenue, returning to government.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he left office for mourning. After three months he was again summoned to oversee Secretariat affairs and concurrently judge the Ministry of Revenue, returning to power.

sentences.zh: 累封須昌縣伯，遷黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly enfeoffed as Baron of Xuchang and moved to Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly enfeoffed as Baron of Xuchang and promoted to vice director of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 上元初，加同中書門下三品，當賜門戟，或勸諲以兇服受吉賜不宜，諲釋缞拜賜，人譏其失禮。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shangyuan he was given the rank of Third Grade Associate Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery; when he was to receive the gate halberds, some urged that in mourning garb it was improper to accept an auspicious gift; Yin removed his hempen mourning and bowed to receive the gift—people mocked his breach of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shangyuan era he was given the rank of third-grade associate director of the Secretariat-Chancellery. When he was to receive the gate halberds, some urged that it was improper to accept an auspicious gift while in mourning garb. Yin removed his hempen mourning and bowed to receive the gift, and people mocked his breach of ritual.

sentences.zh: 諲引妻之父楚賓為衛尉少卿，楚賓子震為郎官。

translations.literal: Yin brought in his wife's father Chubin as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Guards, and Chubin's son Zhen as a Gentleman of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yin brought in his wife's father Chubin as vice director of the Court of Imperial Guards, and Chubin's son Zhen as a gentleman of the palace.

sentences.zh: 中人馬尚言者，素匿於諲，為人求官，諲奏為藍田尉。

translations.literal: The eunuch Ma Shangyan had long been hidden with Yin; he sought offices for others, and Yin memorialized to make him Wei of Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Ma Shangyan had long been sheltered by Yin. He sought offices for others, and Yin memorialized to appoint him magistrate of Lantian.

sentences.zh: 事覺，帝怒，命敬羽窮治，殺尚言，以其肉賜從官，罷諲為太子賓客。

translations.literal: When the matter was discovered the emperor was angry and ordered Jing Yu to investigate thoroughly; Shangyan was killed and his flesh given to attending officials; Yin was removed and made Guest of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was discovered the emperor was furious and ordered Jing Yu to investigate thoroughly. Shangyan was killed and his flesh given to attending officials. Yin was removed and made guest of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 數月，拜荊州長史、澧朗峽忠等五州節度使。

translations.literal: After several months he was appointed Senior Administrator of Jingzhou and Military Commissioner of the five prefectures Li, Lang, Xia, Zhong, and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: After several months he was appointed senior administrator of Jingzhou and military commissioner of the five prefectures Li, Lang, Xia, Zhong, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 諲始建請荊州置南都，詔可。

translations.literal: Yin was the first to propose establishing a Southern Capital at Jingzhou; an edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was the first to propose establishing a southern capital at Jingzhou, and an edict approved the plan.

sentences.zh: 於是更號江陵府，以諲為尹，置永平軍萬人，遏吳、蜀之沖，以湖南之嶽、潭、郴、道、邵、連，黔中之涪凡七州，隸其道。

translations.literal: Thereupon the name was changed to Jiangling Prefecture, with Yin as Magistrate; the Yongping Army of ten thousand men was established to block the thrust of Wu and Shu; the seven prefectures Yue, Tan, Chen, Dao, Shao, and Lian of Hunan, and Fu of Qianzhong, were placed under his circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The district was thereupon renamed Jiangling Prefecture, with Yin as magistrate. The Yongping Army of ten thousand men was established to block the routes between Wu and Shu. The seven prefectures Yue, Tan, Chen, Dao, Shao, and Lian of Hunan, together with Fu of Qianzhong, were placed under his circuit.

sentences.zh: 初，荊州長史張惟一以衡州蠻酋陳希昂為司馬，督家兵千人自防，惟一親將牟遂金與相忤，希昂率兵至惟一所捕之，惟一懼，斬其首以謝，悉以遂金兵屬之，乃退，自是政一出希昂，後入朝，遷常州刺史，過江陵入謁，諲伏甲擊殺之，誅黨偶數十人，積屍府門，內外震服。

translations.literal: At first Senior Administrator Zhang Weiyi of Jingzhou made the Man chieftain of Hengzhou Chen Xi'ang his Major, supervising a thousand household troops for self-defense; Weiyi's close general Mou Suijin quarreled with him; Xi'ang led troops to Weiyi's place to seize him; Weiyi was afraid, beheaded Suijin's head to apologize, and gave all of Suijin's troops to him, then withdrew; from this government issued entirely from Xi'ang; later he entered court and was moved to Prefect of Changzhou; passing Jiangling he entered to pay respects; Yin set hidden soldiers and struck him dead, executed several tens of his party, piled corpses at the prefectural gate, and within and without were awed into submission.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the senior administrator of Jingzhou, Zhang Weiyi, had appointed Chen Xi'ang, a Man chieftain of Hengzhou, as his major to supervise a thousand household troops for self-defense. Weiyi's close general Mou Suijin quarreled with Xi'ang, who led troops to Weiyi's residence to seize him. Weiyi, in fear, beheaded Suijin to apologize and gave all of Suijin's troops to Xi'ang, who then withdrew. From that point government issued entirely from Xi'ang. Later Xi'ang entered court and was transferred to prefect of Changzhou. Passing Jiangling he came to pay respects, but Yin set hidden soldiers and killed him, executed several dozen of his followers, and piled corpses at the prefectural gate. The region was awed into submission.

sentences.zh: 妖人申泰芝用左道事李輔國，擢諫議大夫，置軍邵、道二州間，以泰芝總之，納群蠻金，賞以緋紫，出褚中詔書賜衣示之，群蠻怵於賞，而財不足，更為剽掠，吏不敢制。

translations.literal: The sorcerer Shen Taizhi used heterodox ways to serve Li Fuguo and was promoted to Remonstrating Censor; armies were placed between Shao and Dao prefectures with Taizhi in overall charge; he collected gold from the various Man tribes, rewarded them with crimson and purple, produced imperial edicts from his sleeve to bestow robes and show them; the Man tribes were awed by rewards yet their wealth was insufficient, and they turned again to plunder—officials did not dare restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: The sorcerer Shen Taizhi used heterodox practices to serve Li Fuguo and was promoted to remonstrating censor. Armies were placed between Shao and Dao prefectures with Taizhi in overall charge. He collected gold from various Man tribes, rewarded them with crimson and purple robes, and produced imperial edicts from his sleeve to bestow clothing upon them. The Man tribes were awed by the rewards, but when their wealth proved insufficient they turned again to plunder, and officials did not dare restrain them.

sentences.zh: 潭州刺史龐承鼎疾其奸，因泰芝過潭，縛付吏，劾贓鉅萬，得左道讖記，並奏之。

translations.literal: Prefect of Tanzhou Pang Chengdin hated his wickedness; when Taizhi passed through Tan he bound him and handed him to officials, impeached him for bribes of tens of thousands, obtained heterodox prognostications, and memorialized all together.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Chengdin, prefect of Tanzhou, hated his wickedness. When Taizhi passed through Tan, Chengdin bound him and handed him to officials, impeached him for bribes amounting to tens of thousands, obtained heterodox prognostications, and memorialized the entire case.

sentences.zh: 輔國矯追泰芝還京，既召見，反譖承鼎陷不辜，詔諲按罪。

translations.literal: Fuguo forged an order to recall Taizhi to the capital; once he was summoned and seen, he in turn slandered Chengdin for framing the innocent; an edict ordered Yin to investigate the crime.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo forged an order recalling Taizhi to the capital. Once Taizhi was summoned and received audience, he slandered Chengdin for framing the innocent. An edict ordered Yin to investigate the case.

sentences.zh: 諲使判官嚴郢具獄，暴泰芝惡。

translations.literal: Yin sent his Administrative Aide Yan Ying to complete the case file and expose Taizhi's evils.
translations.idiomatic: Yin sent his administrative aide Yan Ying to complete the case file and expose Taizhi's crimes.

sentences.zh: 帝不省，賜承鼎死，流郢建州。

translations.literal: The emperor did not understand; he granted Chengdin death and exiled Ying to Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not understand the matter. He sentenced Chengdin to death and exiled Ying to Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 後泰芝終以贓徙死，承鼎追原其誣。

translations.literal: Later Taizhi in the end died in exile for bribery; Chengdin was posthumously cleared of the false charge.
translations.idiomatic: Later Taizhi ultimately died in exile for bribery, and Chengdin was posthumously cleared of the false charge.

sentences.zh: 諲為治，不急細務，決大事剛果不撓。

translations.literal: In governing, Yin did not press minor affairs; in deciding great matters he was firm, resolute, and unyielding.
translations.idiomatic: In governing, Yin did not press minor affairs, but in deciding great matters he was firm, resolute, and unyielding.

sentences.zh: 始在河西，悉知諸將能否，及為尹，奏取材者數十人總牙兵，故威惠兩行。

translations.literal: When he was first in Hexi he fully knew which generals could or could not perform; when he became Magistrate he memorialized to select several tens of capable men to command the guard troops, and so both authority and kindness were exercised.
translations.idiomatic: When he was first in Hexi he fully knew which generals could or could not perform. As magistrate he memorialized to select several dozen capable men to command the guard troops, and so both authority and kindness were exercised.

sentences.zh: 諲之相，與李揆不平，既斥，乃用善治聞。

translations.literal: When Yin was chancellor he was at odds with Li Kui; once removed, he became known for skill in governing.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin served as chancellor he was at odds with Li Kui. Once removed from the capital, he became known for skill in governing.

sentences.zh: 揆恐帝復用，即妄奏置軍湖南非便，又陰遣人刺諲過失。

translations.literal: Kui feared the emperor would reuse him and at once falsely memorialized that establishing armies in Hunan was inconvenient, and also secretly sent men to probe Yin's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Kui feared the emperor would recall him and at once falsely memorialized that establishing armies in Hunan was inexpedient. He also secretly sent men to probe Yin's faults.

sentences.zh: 諲上疏訟其事，帝怒，逐揆出之，顯條其罪。

translations.literal: Yin submitted a memorial to sue over the matter; the emperor was angry, expelled Kui from office, and openly listed his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Yin submitted a memorial accusing Kui of the matter. The emperor was angry, expelled Kui from office, and openly listed his crimes.

sentences.zh: 諲苦羸疾，卒，年五十一，贈吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Yin suffered from wasting illness and died at fifty-one; posthumously he was given Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Yin suffered from wasting illness and died at fifty-one. He was posthumously honored as director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 諲在朝不稱任職相，及為荊州，號令明，賦斂均一。

translations.literal: Yin in court did not match the office of chancellor; when he became magistrate of Jingzhou, his orders were clear and tax levies uniform.
translations.idiomatic: Yin did not distinguish himself as chancellor at court, but as magistrate of Jingzhou his orders were clear and tax levies uniform.

sentences.zh: 其治尚威信，故軍士用命，闔境無盜賊，民歌詠之。

translations.literal: His government valued authority and trust, and so soldiers obeyed orders; throughout the circuit there were no bandits or robbers, and the people sang praises of him.
translations.idiomatic: His government valued authority and trust, so soldiers obeyed orders, bandits vanished throughout the circuit, and the people sang his praises.

sentences.zh: 自至德以來，處方面數十人，諲最有名。

translations.literal: From Zhide onward, of the several tens who held regional posts, Yin was the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: From the Zhide era onward, among the several dozen men who held regional posts, Yin was the most renowned.

sentences.zh: 荊人生構房祠，及歿，吏裒錢十萬徙祠府西。

translations.literal: The people of Jing built a shrine to him in life; when he died, officials collected a hundred thousand in cash and moved the shrine west of the prefectural office.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Jing built a shrine to him while he was still alive. After his death officials collected a hundred thousand strings of cash and moved the shrine west of the prefectural office.

sentences.zh: 始，諲知杜鴻漸、元載才，薦於朝，後皆為宰相。

translations.literal: At the beginning Yin recognized the talent of Du Hongjian and Yuan Zai, recommended them to court, and later both became chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Yin recognized the talent of Du Hongjian and Yuan Zai, recommended them to court, and both later became chancellors.

sentences.zh: 永泰中，嚴郢以故吏請謚有司，博士獨孤及謚曰「肅」，郢以故事宰相謚皆二名，請益曰「忠肅」。

translations.literal: In the Yongtai era Yan Ying, as a former subordinate, requested a posthumous title from the authorities; Erudite Dugu Ji gave the title Su; Ying, citing precedent that chancellors' posthumous titles were all two characters, requested addition to make Zhongsu.
