translations.idiomatic: During the Yongtai era Yan Ying, as a former subordinate, requested a posthumous title from the authorities. Erudite Dugu Ji proposed Su. Ying, citing precedent that chancellors' posthumous titles were always two characters, requested that it be expanded to Zhongsu.

sentences.zh: 及執奏，謂：「謚在義美惡，不在多名。

translations.literal: When he presented the memorial he said: "Posthumous titles lie in the meaning of good and evil, not in many names.
translations.idiomatic: When he presented the memorial he argued, "Posthumous titles rest on the meaning of good and evil, not on multiplying names.

sentences.zh: 文王伐崇，周公殺三監、淮夷，重耳一戰而霸，而謚曰文。

translations.literal: King Wen attacked Chong; the Duke of Zhou killed the Three Overseers and the Huaiyi; Chong'er with one battle became hegemon—yet their posthumous titles were Wen.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen attacked Chong; the Duke of Zhou killed the Three Overseers and the Huaiyi; Chong'er with a single battle became hegemon—yet their posthumous titles were Wen.

sentences.zh: 冀缺之恪，寧俞之忠，隨會不忘其君，而謚曰武。

translations.literal: Ji Que's reverence, Ning Yu's loyalty, and Sui Hui's not forgetting his lord—yet their posthumous titles were Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Que's reverence, Ning Yu's loyalty, and Sui Hui's fidelity to his lord—yet their posthumous titles were Wu.

sentences.zh: 故知稱其大、略其細也。

translations.literal: Thus one knows that titles praise the great and pass over the small.
translations.idiomatic: Thus one knows that titles praise what is great and pass over what is small.

sentences.zh: 且二名謚，非古也。

translations.literal: Moreover, two-character posthumous titles are not ancient.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, two-character posthumous titles are not ancient practice.

sentences.zh: 漢興，蕭何、張良、霍去病、霍光以文武大略，佐漢致太平，一名不盡其善，乃有文終、文成、景桓、宣成之謚。

translations.literal: When Han arose, Xiao He, Zhang Liang, Huo Qubing, and Huo Guang, with civil and military grand strategy, assisted Han to reach great peace—one character could not exhaust their goodness, and so there were the posthumous titles Wenzong, Wencheng, Jinghuan, and Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Han arose, Xiao He, Zhang Liang, Huo Qubing, and Huo Guang, with grand civil and military strategy, assisted Han to reach great peace. A single character could not exhaust their virtues, and so there arose posthumous titles such as Wenzong, Wencheng, Jinghuan, and Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 唐興，參用漢制，魏徵以王道佐時近『文』，愛君忘身近『貞』，二者並優，廢一莫可，故曰文貞。

translations.literal: When Tang arose it adopted Han institutions; Wei Zheng, in assisting the age with the kingly way, was close to "Wen"; in loving the ruler and forgetting self, close to "Zhen"—both excellences together, abandoning one was impossible, and so it was called Wenzhen.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang arose it adopted Han institutions. Wei Zheng, in assisting the age with the kingly way, was close to Wen; in loving the ruler and forgetting self, close to Zhen. Both excellences stood together and neither could be abandoned, and so he was called Wenzhen.

sentences.zh: 蕭瑀端直近『貞』，性多猜近『褊』，言『褊』則失『貞』，稱『貞』則遺『褊』，故曰貞褊。

translations.literal: Xiao Yu was upright and close to "Zhen," yet by nature suspicious and close to "Pian"—to speak "Pian" would lose "Zhen," to call "Zhen" would omit "Pian," and so it was called Zhenpian.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yu was upright and close to Zhen, yet by nature suspicious and close to Pian. To speak Pian would lose Zhen; to call Zhen would omit Pian. Hence he was called Zhenpian.

sentences.zh: 蓋有為為之也。

translations.literal: These were all done with deliberate purpose.
translations.idiomatic: These were all done with deliberate purpose.

sentences.zh: 若跡無異稱，則易以一字。

translations.literal: If the record had no exceptional praise, then a single character would suffice.
translations.idiomatic: If the record had no exceptional praise, a single character would suffice.

sentences.zh: 故杜如晦曰成，封德彜曰明，王珪曰懿，陳叔達曰忠，溫彥博曰恭，岑文本曰憲，韋世源曰昭，皆當時赫赫居宰相位者，謚不過一名。

translations.literal: Thus Du Ruhui was called Cheng, Feng Deyi Ming, Wang Gui Yi, Chen Shuda Zhong, Wen Yanbo Gong, Cen Wende Xian, Wei Shiyuan Zhao—all at the time illustrious in the chancellor's seat, their posthumous titles no more than one character.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Du Ruhui was called Cheng, Feng Deyi Ming, Wang Gui Yi, Chen Shuda Zhong, Wen Yanbo Gong, Cen Wende Xian, and Wei Shiyuan Zhao—all illustrious chancellors of their day whose posthumous titles were no more than a single character.

sentences.zh: 而言故事宰相必以二名，固所未聞。

translations.literal: Yet to say that by precedent chancellors must have two names is something never heard of.
translations.idiomatic: To say that by precedent chancellors must have two-character titles is something never heard of.

sentences.zh: 宜如前謚。

translations.literal: It is fitting to follow the earlier posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: The earlier proposed title should stand.

sentences.zh: 」遂不改。

translations.literal: " Thereupon it was not changed.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon it was not changed.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：孔子稱才難。

translations.literal: The Praise says: Confucius said that talent is hard to find.
translations.idiomatic: The Praise says: Confucius said that talent is hard to find.

sentences.zh: 然人之才有限，不得皆善。

translations.literal: Yet human talent has limits and cannot all be good.
translations.idiomatic: Yet human talent has limits, and not everyone can excel in every way.

sentences.zh: 觀圓之銳，而失守出奔；

translations.literal: Consider Yuan's keenness, yet he lost his post and fled;
translations.idiomatic: Consider Yuan's keen ambition, yet he lost his post and fled;

sentences.zh: 晉卿雅厚，而少風采臧否；

translations.literal: Jinqing was refined and generous, yet lacked spirit in judging right and wrong;
translations.idiomatic: Jinqing was refined and generous, yet lacked spirit in judging right and wrong;

sentences.zh: 冕明強，嗜利不知大體；

translations.literal: Mian was bright and forceful, loving profit and ignorant of the great substance;
translations.idiomatic: Mian was bright and forceful, greedy for profit and ignorant of larger responsibilities;

sentences.zh: 諲輔政，功名不及治郡。

translations.literal: Yin assisted in government, yet fame and merit did not match his governing a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yin assisted in government, yet his fame and achievement as chancellor did not match his success in governing a commandery.

sentences.zh: 然各以所長顯於時。

translations.literal: Yet each displayed in his age what he did best.
translations.idiomatic: Yet each displayed in his age what he did best.

sentences.zh: 故聖人使人也器之，不窮所不能而後為治也。

translations.literal: Therefore the sage in employing men treats them as vessels, not exhausting what they cannot do and only then governing.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the sage employs men according to their capacities, not exhausting what they cannot do and only then governing.

sentences.zh: 遵慶寡疵，中人之賢與。

translations.literal: Zunqing had few flaws—he was the worth of an average man.
translations.idiomatic: Zunqing had few flaws—he was the worth of a capable but unexceptional man.
